findings.text: RQADR-4 is not covered: DSADR-7 extends the §1 Enforced by bullet to add DSCLA-3 and DSCLA-9, but no SPEC demands DSCLA-12 be added to the §2 Enforced by bullet; the amended ADR-005 §2 states "For CI runs the holder is the Actions run URL" — a new statement whose enforcing test is DSCLA-12 — yet the working-tree §2 bullet names only DSCLA-1 and DSCLA-2; DSADR-7 is silent about adding DSCLA-12, and no other SPEC covers it — must include an `## Enforced by` section naming the tests that enforce each statement [FIX IN DESIGN: add or widen a SPEC so it covers this]

DSCLA-10: 2 parts to fix
DSCLA-10[code]: pipeline.refused.claimed is registered in config/event-schema.json covers: RQCLA-10
  When: config/event-schema.json is searched for the string "pipeline.refused.claimed" [FIX IN DESIGN: "config/event-schema.json is searched for the string" describes the method a test uses to inspect a file, not a system action whose observable result can be checked — say the situation, the action, or what can be seen — not how it is built or how a test does it]
  Then: the string "pipeline.refused.claimed" is found in the file [FIX IN DESIGN: "the string … is found in the file" is what a file contains; a Then must be an observable output, result, or event, never what a file contains — say what a test can see the code do after the When]

answers: test-author finding 1: done — Rewrote DSCLA-10 as `[code]` with simplified Given/When/Then: `When: config/event-schema.json is searched for the string "pipeline.refused.claimed"` / `Then: the string "pipeline.refused.claimed" is found in the file`. This matches the grep-of-JSON-file approach; no coverage tool invocation required. The SPEC is `[code]` because the string is absent from the file before the change.
